start_here_rows: Application: What do you do with the tent peg?
start_here_runtime: 57 minutes with the full response; 55–60 with normal variation. The manuscript is 6,955 words at about 120 words per minute.
start_here_cut: If you have 50 minutes: Introduction to 4, Movement 1 to 6, Movement 2 to 6, Movement 3 to 7, Movement 4 to 7, Movement 5 to 7, Application to 5. Keep the prophecy of 4:9, “the LORD routed,” the peg, Judges 5:24, and Colossians 2:13–15.
start_here_guardrails: Do not glamorize the killing. Name the deception and the broken treaty; Jael is God’s instrument in this war, not a model for private revenge.
Do not make Jael or Deborah a culture-war mascot. The point is God’s deliverance through the unlikely.
Preach the violence with pastoral care. The sermon is not a command to take vengeance; provide a care note for victims of violence and abuse.
Keep the typology modest. Genesis 3:15 is an echo, not a direct prophecy; the tent peg is not a prophecy of the nails.
Do not despise Barak. Hebrews 11:32 names him among the faithful; his is a weak faith that still obeys.
The gospel must be explicit: Colossians 2:13–15 and the resurrection. Do not end on “be brave.”
start_here_evidence: The 900 iron chariots, the Kishon rout, the Kenite treaty, and the tent peg are doing theological work, and the cross and empty tomb are the turn.

slides.run: A SERMON FOR THE PULPIT · 55–60 MINUTES

slides.label: 01 · THE BIG IDEA
lines: Jael drove a peg through the enemy.
Jesus took the nails for us.
slides.note: God wins through the unlikely. The victory is His.

slides.label: 03 · THE CALL
slides.headline: A prophetess, a general, a promise.
panel: The glory would go to the unlikely.

slides.label: 04 · THE BATTLE
slides.headline: The LORD routed Sisera.
slides.body: Deborah cried, “Up! For this is the day in which the LORD has given Sisera into your hand.” Barak went down from Tabor, and the LORD routed the army. The stars fought. The river swept. Not a man was left.
slides.pullquote: Does not the LORD go out before you?
slides.footline: The victory was not Barak’s. It was the LORD’s.

slides.label: 05 · THE OPEN DOOR
slides.headline: He ran to the wrong tent.
slides.quote: “Turn aside, my lord; turn aside to me; do not be afraid.”
slides.aside1: A treaty of peace. A woman alone.
slides.aside2: He asked for water. She gave him milk. He asked her to lie.
slides.footline: He thought he had found shelter. He had walked into the hand of God.

slides.label: 06 · THE PEG
slides.footline: A woman, a peg, and the God who wins through the unlikely.

slides.label: 07 · THE SONG
slides.banner_main: “Most blessed of women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, of tent-dwelling women most blessed.”
slides.footline: Blessed is the one who answers, not the one the world expects.

slides.label: 08 · BLESSED AMONG WOMEN
slides.banner_main: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!”
lines: Jael drove a peg into the enemy.
Jesus took the nails for his enemies.
slides.footline: One woman ended a war. One Son ended the war with God.

slides.label: 09 · THE RESPONSE
slides.headline: What do you do with the tent peg?

title: Do not wait
for the perfect moment.
items.desc: Act in the window God gives you. Obedience is often an interruption.

title: Do not mistake
peace for passivity.
items.desc: Comfort is not the same as faithfulness. False peace is still a cage.

title: Use what is
in your hand.
items.desc: A peg, a hammer, a home, a story. Offer the ordinary to God.

title: Give the victory
to God.
items.desc: The stars fought. The river swept. The LORD won. Let Him have the glory.

slides.footline: The LORD does not need a chariot. He needs a willing hand.

slides.label: 10 · THE INVITATION
slides.line1: Not because you are strong. Because he is.
lines: Jesus’ cross ended the war that mattered.
